claim_summary: TSFLab contributes an agent-agnostic workbench that provides forecasting research guidance, structured temporal knowledge, shared experiment execution, and verified maintenance of reusable research resources.

claim_evidence.quote: propose TSFLab, a self-improving agent-agnostic “workbench” that equips compatible coding agents with shared resources and tools for low-cost TSF research and continuous maintenance of research resources.

modules.name: Forecasting research guide and task-specific skills
modules.scope_reason: R3.1 TSK: the guide encodes forecasting workflows and protocol checks; changing the task family requires replacing forecast-specific targets and evaluation checks. R3.2 GTS is insufficient because the guide embeds a forecasting task procedure, and R3.3 GH is too general because the procedure is task-bound.
rubric_path: R1:contributed
R2:Harness
R3_1_TSK:yes - forecasting workflow and evaluation checks are task-bound

evidence.quote: For example, when benchmarking methods on a new dataset, a skill guides the agent to identify time fields, forecasting variables, sampling frequency, and evaluation settings, then register data through the workbench’s “add” interface and inspect partitioning and scaling through its “split” interface.

modules.name: Progressively disclosed method and dataset knowledge cards
modules.scope_reason: R3.2 GTS: cards organize temporal dataset and method properties such as frequency, protocols, and model parameters, while the retrieval structure is not bound to a forecasting output objective. Another time-series task can use the same catalog mechanism with different resources; R3.1 TSK is not met, and R3.3 GH misses the temporal metadata in its state.
rubric_path: R1:contributed
R2:Harness
R3_1_TSK:no - card retrieval does not encode a forecast output criterion
R3_2_GTS:yes - cards preserve temporal dataset and method properties

evidence.quote: It provides a knowledge card for each method, dataset, and unit, organized into summary, card, and source levels. Summaries support screening; cards describe capabilities, parameters, interfaces, and limitations; sources provide papers, reference code, and detailed explanations.

modules.name: Importable shared time-series model units
modules.scope_reason: R3.2 GTS: reusable units such as normalization, decomposition, and attention operate on temporal series structure, but do not encode a particular forecast output criterion. They remain useful across time-series tasks, whereas changing to non-temporal inputs would require redesigning their interfaces; R3.1 TSK and R3.3 GH therefore do not fit.
rubric_path: R1:contributed
R2:Harness
R3_1_TSK:no - units do not embed one task objective
R3_2_GTS:yes - unit computation operates on temporal series
R3_3_GH:no - the units have temporal input assumptions

evidence.quote: Knowledge Structurer also extracts common blocks, such as RevIN, series decomposition, and attention variants, into shared units that methods import, enabling shared maintenance; 263 methods reuse at least one unit.

modules.name: Temporal data registration, splitting, and validation
modules.scope_reason: R3.2 GTS: the shared routines manage chronological data splits and train-only scaling, which depend on temporal information and remain useful across time-series task families. They do not themselves define the forecast objective required by R3.1 TSK; R3.3 GH would omit the temporal data constraints.
rubric_path: R1:contributed
R2:Harness
R3_1_TSK:no - the data operations do not encode a forecast output criterion
R3_2_GTS:yes - the operations depend on temporal splits and data availability

evidence.quote: Shared routines split data as configured, fit scaling on training data only, select checkpoints on validation data, and compute metrics consistently.

modules.name: Declarative experiment runner under shared forecasting protocols
modules.scope_reason: R3.1 TSK: the runner organizes experiments around forecasting lookback, horizon, and training budgets. Changing the task family requires redesigning the task configuration and evaluation procedure; temporal semantics alone (R3.2 GTS) do not capture the forecast-specific experiment contract, and the runner is more than generic scheduling (R3.3 GH).
rubric_path: R1:contributed
R2:Harness
R3_1_TSK:yes - experiment configuration and evaluation are forecasting-specific

evidence.quote: Agents use Compose to combine presets, Override to change settings, and Sweep to expand methods or values. For new-data benchmarking, an agent combines dataset and method presets, fixes the lookback, horizon, and training budget, and sweeps methods and seeds.

modules.name: Verified maintenance of shared research resources
modules.scope_reason: R3.3 GH: the core mechanism screens and integrates resource updates through usability, complexity, and consistency checks. Its update cycle remains applicable if the task family changes, while temporal or task-specific checks can be supplied by the resources; it does not itself depend on temporal order or embed a forecast objective, so R3.1 TSK and R3.2 GTS do not apply.
rubric_path: R1:contributed
R2:Harness
R3_1_TSK:no - it does not encode a task output criterion
R3_2_GTS:no - its update and CI lifecycle is not temporal-state dependent
R3_3_GH:yes - it manages shared resource verification and integration

evidence.quote: Recursive Improver brings external resources and agent-produced outcomes back into the shared workbench through checks for usability, complexity, and consistency (Fig. 2d). Failed checks prompt revision and rechecking before integration, supporting workbench maintenance.

process_validity.quote: A session is accepted if it covers the complete requested matrix with executed metrics, the prescribed splits, train-only scaling, the common evaluation over all windows, and no test-informed configuration selection;

temporal_validity.quote: Data. Chronological 70/10/20 split; train-only scaling; all channels; input 168 and horizon 24.

task_performance.quote: On ETTh1 and Weather (Fig. 3b,c), TSFLab reaches the lowest test MSE with less time and fewer fresh tokens than every other setting; details are in App. D.

reconciliation.reason: The paper's concrete contributions are its separately described modules; the umbrella workbench label restates the system without an independent mechanism and duplicates those modules.

changes: dimensions: Planning and Workflow -> Planning and Orchestration
reconciliation.reason: Keep the forecasting task procedure and its id; update the retired dimension label and record the temporal data and protocol checks described in the guide.

Keep the card catalog under its existing id and split out the independently importable shared code units; cards retain temporal resource properties but neither mechanism is tied to a single forecast output criterion.

changes: dimensions: Control, Verification, and Feedback -> Planning and Orchestration
reconciliation.reason: The shared temporal split, scaling, and validation mechanism remains distinct from experiment orchestration and maps to the current temporal layer and dimension vocabulary.

changes: dimensions: Planning and Workflow -> Planning and Orchestration; Control, Verification, and Feedback -> Planning and Orchestration
reconciliation.reason: Keep the experiment runner as a forecasting-bound task procedure; map its orchestration and execution dimensions to the current vocabulary.

changes: dimensions: Control, Verification, and Feedback -> Planning and Orchestration
reconciliation.reason: Keep the generic resource update and verification cycle in GH; retain its evolution function and map the in-episode checks to the current planning dimension.

notes: The existing umbrella module duplicates the separately supported workbench components. The combined cards-and-units entry is split because card retrieval and importable model code are independently reusable mechanisms. Layer of knowledge-cards is a close call (cards describe forecasting methods and protocols); decided GTS because the card structure is task-neutral.

items.reason: The three-level summary/card/source catalogue stores dataset cards recording data characteristics and split, scaling and evaluation protocols plus method/unit cards; the mechanism embeds no forecast output criterion or verifier, and the temporal dataset metadata fails GH (R3.1 no, R3.2 yes). Forecast-specific content is resource content, not the mechanism; task membership does not decide scope.
Units such as RevIN and series decomposition are extracted into importable blocks with their own cards and maintained separately from the card catalogue.

adjudication.summary: The candidate was checked against Sections 3.2-3.5 and accepted unchanged. The only layer move (knowledge-cards TSK->GTS) satisfies R3.2 and not R3.1.
